THE SERMON OF THE SALT-BLIND LEVIATHAN

SPOKEN BENEATH THE ASHEN BELL

Attend, ash-breathed faithful, and lower your faces from the wind.

There is a creature beneath the world's white scars whose coming is
not heralded by trumpet, nor by banner, nor by the shining of
watchfires. It is called the Salt-Blind Leviathan. Remember the
name, not because names grant safety, but because a named terror may
be faced without pretending it is merely weather.

The Salt-Blind Leviathan is a siege-breaker of moderate threat. Let
no fool mock the word moderate. A measured blade may still open the
throat. A contained fire may still consume the storehouse.
"Moderate" does not mean harmless. It means only that the terror has
been weighed by minds that survived the weighing.

Look upon its likeness in the salt-marked stones: a vast leviathan,
its features pale and crusted with salt, its eyes sightless. It
cannot trust the road by seeing it. It cannot judge the wall by the
glint upon its stones. It cannot follow a torch, nor be turned aside
by a painted decoy. The Salt-Blind Leviathan is defined by an
inability to rely on sight.

And yet it advances.

This is the lesson the proud refuse. We praise the eye because the
eye flatters us. We believe what we see, and we mistake what we see
for all that is true. But the Salt-Blind Leviathan does not need the
face of the fortress. It knows the fortress through pressure. It
finds the gate by resistance. It learns the wall by the sound of its
breaking.

Its force is immense destructive force. Its burden is not a sudden
rage, but a weight that does not cease. Its demeanor conveys
ponderous, relentless pressure. Mark those words upon your hearts:
ponderous, relentless pressure. Not haste. Not frenzy. The mountain
does not hurry when it crushes the buried house.

Therefore, when the Salt-Blind Leviathan comes, do not waste your
strength crying that it cannot see you. It does not need to see you.
Do not boast that your walls are tall. Height is only another
measure of falling stone. Do not beg the darkness to hide you.

Darkness is no blindness to the thing that was born without sight.

Stand soberly. Brace what may be braced. Carry away what may be
carried. Let the proud hear the grinding beneath the earth and
understand: not every warning arrives as a voice.

The Salt-Blind Leviathan is no demon to be flattered, no beast to be
shamed, no storm to be cursed into silence. It is the pressure that
comes, and comes, and comes.

Pray, then—not for its eyes to open.

Pray for your hearts not to close.
